data.title: Alpha HPA Insiders Recover Some Losses, Which Stand At AU$42k
data.description:
Some of the losses seen by insiders who purchased AU$124.1k worth of Alpha HPA Limited (ASX:A4N) shares over the past year were recovered after the stock increased by 15% over the past week. However, the purchase is proving to be an expensive wager as insiders are yet to get ahead of their losses which currently stand at AU$42k since the time of purchase.

While insider transactions are not the most important thing when it comes to long-term investing, we do think it is perfectly logical to keep tabs on what insiders are doing.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

The Last 12 Months Of Insider Transactions At Alpha HPA

The MD & Director Robert Williamson made the biggest insider purchase in the last 12 months. That single transaction was for AU$80k worth of shares at a price of AU$0.53 each. That means that even when the share price was higher than AU$0.35 (the recent price), an insider wanted to purchase shares. Their view may have changed since then, but at least it shows they felt optimistic at the time. We always take careful note of the price insiders pay when purchasing shares. As a general rule, we feel more positive about a stock if insiders have bought shares at above current prices, because that suggests they viewed the stock as good value, even at a higher price.

While Alpha HPA insiders bought shares during the last year, they didn't sell. The chart below shows insider transactions (by companies and individuals) over the last year. By clicking on the graph below, you can see the precise details of each insider transaction!

See our latest analysis for Alpha HPA

Alpha HPA is not the only stock that insiders are buying. For those who like to find small cap companies at attractive valuations, this free list of growing companies with recent insider purchasing, could be just the ticket.

Insider Ownership Of Alpha HPA

I like to look at how many shares insiders own in a company, to help inform my view of how aligned they are with insiders. I reckon it's a good sign if insiders own a significant number of shares in the company. It appears that Alpha HPA insiders own 6.0% of the company, worth about AU$31m. We've certainly seen higher levels of insider ownership elsewhere, but these holdings are enough to suggest alignment between insiders and the other shareholders.

What Might The Insider Transactions At Alpha HPA Tell Us?

There haven't been any insider transactions in the last three months -- that doesn't mean much. However, our analysis of transactions over the last year is heartening. Insiders own shares in Alpha HPA and we see no evidence to suggest they are worried about the future. So these insider transactions can help us build a thesis about the stock, but it's also worthwhile knowing the risks facing this company. For instance, we've identified 4 warning signs for Alpha HPA (2 don't sit too well with us) you should be aware of.

Of course Alpha HPA may not be the best stock to buy. So you may wish to see this free collection of high quality companies.

For the purposes of this article, insiders are those individuals who report their transactions to the relevant regulatory body. We currently account for open market transactions and private dispositions of direct interests only, but not derivative transactions or indirect interests.

data.title: Earnings Upgrades Might Change The Case For Investing In TI Stock
data.description:
• Texas Instruments has pushed ahead with large scale U.S. manufacturing expansion, including RFAB2 in Richardson, LFAB1 in Lehi, and SM1 in Sherman, while earnings estimates for the current year have been revised higher by 7.6% in the last 60 days.
  • The combination of long lived analog product demand and heavier near term depreciation from these new fabs is putting the spotlight on how effectively Texas Instruments can turn this buildout into sustainable cash generation rather than just headline capacity.
  • Next, the focus shifts to how Texas Instruments' manufacturing centric moat interacts with these earnings upgrades to reshape the investment narrative.

Texas Instruments Investment Narrative Recap

To own Texas Instruments, you need to believe its manufacturing focused moat in long lived analog chips can keep turning a very broad product catalog into steady cash generation, even as cycles shift. According to OLetourneau, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community, the real edge is cost efficient 300mm fabs and decades long product lifecycles. The key near term catalyst is how quickly those new U.S. plants move from heavy spend and depreciation into solid utilization, which the recent earnings estimate upgrades point toward without changing the basic execution test.

The biggest operational risk right now sits in the same place. Large new fabs mean higher fixed costs, so any period of softer demand or slower industrial and auto orders could pressure margins while the capacity ramps. Depreciation and capital intensity do not derail the Texas Instruments story on their own, but they can compress reported earnings for a while if volumes lag expectations, which matters for a stock already trading on a relatively full P/E.

The clearest tie between the current news flow and the long term story is the U.S. manufacturing buildout, especially RFAB2 in Richardson, LFAB1 in Lehi, and SM1 in Sherman. That build is what turns OLetourneau’s view of 300mm cost leadership into something you can track in real time through utilization, unit costs, and cash conversion. Recent estimate upgrades and analyst visits simply direct attention back to whether those sites come online at the cost and yield levels management is targeting.

These facilities also intersect directly with income oriented investors watching Texas Instruments for its dividend and cash returns. Higher capex and depreciation compete with shareholder payouts if free cash flow tightens, so the ramp profile of RFAB2, LFAB1, and SM1 effectively acts as both a catalyst and a risk. If execution stays on plan, the expanded in house production can reinforce pricing on those long lived analog SKUs. If ramp timing or demand proves weaker, the heavier asset base can weigh on reported profitability for longer than the recent estimate revisions imply.

On OLetourneau’s numbers, that US$284.32 fair value for Texas Instruments lines up with a model that assumes revenue expanding at 14.2% a year and future profit margin settling at 30.0%, which effectively prices in strong analog demand flowing through those newer 300mm fabs.

We note that the Capral Limited (ASX:CAA) MD, CEO & Non Independent Director, Anthony Dragicevich, recently sold AU$113k worth of stock for AU$12.38 per share. On the bright side, that's just a small sale and only reduced their holding by 1.7%.

Capral Insider Transactions Over The Last Year

Notably, that recent sale by MD, CEO & Non Independent Director Anthony Dragicevich was not the only time they sold Capral shares this year. They previously made an even bigger sale of -AU$593k worth of shares at a price of AU$11.85 per share. So it's clear an insider wanted to take some cash off the table, even below the current price of AU$13.05. We generally consider it a negative if insiders have been selling, especially if they did so below the current price, because it implies that they considered a lower price to be reasonable. Please do note, however, that sellers may have a variety of reasons for selling, so we don't know for sure what they think of the stock price. We usually like to see fairly high levels of insider ownership. From our data, it seems that Capral insiders own 4.3% of the company, worth about AU$8.8m. We do generally prefer see higher levels of insider ownership.

What Might The Insider Transactions At Capral Tell Us?

An insider sold stock recently, but they haven't been buying. Despite some insider buying, the longer term picture doesn't make us feel much more positive. The market may be focusing on the headline of “drones” rather than the quieter test of whether Ford can reliably monetize its industrial footprint outside autos while GM and others chase similar contracts.

There is a flip side. Defense customers care about quality, delivery and IP discipline, and analysts have already flagged warranty, recall and legal risks at Ford Motor. Any Pentagon role that goes beyond prototypes would make those execution questions more visible, and weak delivery here would challenge the idea that cleaner capital deployment and cost control are really taking hold.

In practice, this drone story only matters to you in the context of which Ford Motor Narrative you believe. The same headline either reinforces a multi platform manufacturing bet or underlines the execution risks that could derail it.

data.title: What Has Changed For XPeng Since Its 59% Fall
data.description:
XPeng has just rolled out what it calls China’s first mass-produced Robotaxi built on in-house Level 4 autonomous tech, a headline-grabbing step in its Physical AI push. Investors who held XPeng over the past year are down 58.8%, including dividends. That result reflects every hope and worry baked in since late 2025. If you had been weighing a position back then, how should this Robotaxi milestone reshape what you expect from the core auto business and margins now?

The useful thing about a Narrative is that the reasoning is checkable: the assumptions sit beside the argument, and together they imply an estimated Fair Value you can disagree with.

This theme extends beyond XPeng. See which of 94 robotics and automation stocks may still merit a closer look.

What XPeng Investors Were Really Arguing About

The shares cost US$20.79 at the start of the period. Anyone looking at XPeng then had to choose between two very different stories about what that price already assumed.

The bullish narrative saw Fair Value at US$26.29, based on XPeng using international expansion and partnerships to support revenue growth of 31.6% a year and a future profit margin of 4.6%.

The bearish view put Fair Value at US$18.06 and focused on global EV rivalry. This narrative highlighted pricing pressure, regulatory risks around tariffs, and rising compliance costs as threats to margins and cash generation.

What The Evidence Did To The XPeng Argument

XPeng’s launch of a mass-produced Level 4 Robotaxi using in-house hardware and software backed the bullish idea that proprietary tech and Physical AI could matter for pricing power and new revenue streams. The same window showed a tougher reality on the income statement. Revenue in Q3 2026 was CNY 24,276.0m, yet net margin fell from a 1.9% loss to a 3.6% loss. Overall, the evidence cut both ways.

The key lesson is simple. When a story leans on premium tech and new platforms, track whether net margin is actually moving toward profit alongside product milestones, not just whether XPeng or any peer is shipping more units.

What XPeng’s Lower Price Is Asking You To Believe

XPeng trades at US$8.99, so the stock is well below where earlier bulls were arguing, but the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St still places its Fair Value above that level.

The Narrative leans on Physical AI, Robotaxi and overseas EVs sharing one tech stack. That higher figure assumes XPeng eventually turns that shared platform into meaningfully stronger margins.

"XPeng's shift from a pure EV maker to a broader Physical AI group that reuses its in-house chips, models and software across vehicles, Robotaxi and humanoid robots is expected to create multiple revenue streams from a single technology stack and improve long term returns on R&D investment."

One Narrative has put a figure on that disagreement. → See the Narrative with its higher Fair Value, assumptions and all

An XPeng Check One Step Away

XPeng talks about Physical AI and robots moving beyond cars. Another player is chasing that idea from a different angle.

Where XPeng leans on Robotaxi fleets, this other business is pushing humanoid machines as a labour platform. The pitch is simple and software driven.

Sell the robot once, then sell new skills over time. Each software upgrade turns a one-off hardware sale into a repeat service relationship.

That echoes how recurring digital fees changed what a smartphone really was. It turned devices into evolving service hubs instead of static tools.

If XPeng executes on its own platform vision, your reference point might not be old auto makers anymore. It could be whoever turns physical work into a software subscription.

data.title: 3 US Stocks Retail Investors Are Watching As Tariffs Reshape Steel Pricing
data.description:
The new Section 301 tariffs have put trade policy back on center stage, and that shift is already reshaping expectations around US producers that compete with imported steel, aluminium, autos, appliances, and solar equipment. Investors who ignore this turn in policy risk missing where pricing power and pressure may now cluster. This article walks through three stocks exposed to the latest tariff headlines and explains how the news could matter for your portfolio decisions.

The stocks highlighted below are only a small sample, and the full screen surfaced 44 additional companies with equally compelling tariff-linked stories that are not covered in this article. Reliance (RS)

Reliance appears closely aligned with the tariff story, as the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St highlights how its domestic sourcing model and broad metals processing footprint tie directly into shifts in trade policy and supply chains.

Reshoring and domestic purchasing trends are aligning with Reliance sourcing about 95% of its metal from U.S. mills and maintaining low claim relationships. This can support reliable access to material, shorter lead times and more stable earnings in a tight supply and tariff supported pricing environment.

What matters next is how one unresolved pressure on input costs and pricing balance feeds through to margins over the coming quarters.

Reliance, Inc. is a US and Canada focused metal solutions and processing group serving manufacturers and infrastructure projects, earning about US$17.4b from its Metals Service Centers segment and carrying a market value near US$21.2b.

As that margin story unfolds, read the full narrative for Reliance to see how tariff support, capital allocation and cycle risk could be quietly reshaping Reliance.

Steel Dynamics (STLD)

Steel Dynamics is one of the purest plays on US-focused steel and aluminum tariff protection in this screen, and the bullish analyst Narrative on Simply Wall St argues that its mix of mills, recycling and fabrication leaves it especially exposed to any shift in import pressure.

"The aluminum rolling mill has moved from larger start up losses to a Q3 2026 operating loss of US$26 million as shipments reached 53,000 metric tons and quarterly production reached about half of mill capability."

What happens if that early aluminum drag flips into a cleaner profit stream while tariff support keeps domestic steel pricing and utilization tight?

Steel Dynamics is a US steel producer and recycler. Its tariff-aligned steel operations generated about US$15.5b of Steel Operations revenue in the last period, with Metals Recycling at roughly US$4.6b, Steel Fabrication at US$1.6b and Aluminum at about US$1.4b, underpinning a market value near US$30.8b.

Nucor (NUE)

Nucor is one of the clearest tariff-linked stories in this screen, with a primarily US steel footprint that puts it directly in the path of any import duties on foreign metal and feeds a broad mix of mill, products and raw materials demand across construction, manufacturing and energy customers.

Nucor generates most of its money from Steel Mills, which produced about US$30.1b of revenue, with Raw Materials at roughly US$14.9b and Steel Products at around US$12.6b, supporting a market value near US$55.9b.

"The growing role of data centers in Nucor’s backlog, now around 15% at the enterprise level and roughly 30% to 35% of structural backlog, gives the company an opportunity to use its ability to supply about 95% of required steel to increase cross selling across plate, structural, tube and building systems and support revenue growth and mix driven EBITDA."
